title: U2 announces 2027 shows in Toronto, Vancouver as part of world tour
summary: U2 announced the first Canadian dates in its world tour on Tuesday, in support of the new album Carnaval de Luz.

image.caption: Bono, left, and The Edge, right, are shown performing during U2's surprise performance at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Nov. 14. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: U2 announced the first Canadian dates in its world tour on Tuesday, in support of the new album Carnaval de Luz.
Band has not played in Canada since 2018

The Irish superstars will be hitting Canadian cities for the first time in about a decade in 2027, with shows Sept. 7 and Sept. 9 at Rogers Stadium in Toronto and Oct. 18 at BC Place in Vancouver. Stephen Wilson Jr. is scheduled to open for the band in Toronto, with The War on Drugs announced as the opening act in Vancouver.
The band earlier announced dates in Latin America beginning in February to launch the tour, dubbed the Greatest Show on Earth tour.

U2 last played in Canada in 2017-18. The band has an extensive history in the country, with Toronto, Montreal and Ottawa some of the first shows the band ever played outside Europe, in 1980-81 while touring their debut album Boy.
Carnaval de Luz, released on Nov. 13, is the band's 16th studio album.

While the band reworked old favourites for 2023's Songs of Surrender, it's the band's first original collection of songs in nine years. Singles released from the new album have included The Greatest Show on Earth, Street of Dreams and Silencio.

"There will be loud guitars, deep bass, some ecstatic rhythms," singer Bono promised in a statement announcing the album, which was again produced with their frequent collaborator Garret (Jacknife) Lee.
The last track on the album is Torn, a duet with Dolly Parton, who died in August.
The band performed Silencio, along with their classic 1984 song Pride (In the Name of Love), at a surprise appearance earlier this month at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony in Los Angeles.

In addition to the tour, Bono, guitarist The Edge, bassist Adam Clayton and drummer Larry Mullen Jr. will be in the spotlight in 2027 as recipients of the MusiCares persons of the year, the annual honour given during the Grammy Awards weekend in Los Angeles in February.

U2 has supported many causes since forming 50 years ago in Dublin, including global health, disaster response, addiction recovery, mental health and access to music education. MusiCares honoured Bono individually in 2003.
Bono also received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in early 2025 from U.S. President Joe Biden, in recognition of his humanitarian efforts.
With files from the Associated Press
